CORE BC – Power Made Simple
The Seasonic CORE BC Series delivers reliable performance and modern ATX 3.1 compliance at an essential value. Designed for everyday builders and gamers, it embodies Seasonic’s trusted quality in a compact 140 mm design with a durable scratch-resistant finish.
With 80 PLUS® Bronze efficiency, Smart and Silent Fan Control (S2FC), and a 120 mm HDB fan, it ensures cool, quiet, and stable operation. The CORE BC-750 and CORE BC-850 include a 12V-2×6 PCIe Gen 5.1 cable, ready for the latest GPUs, while the CORE BC-650 meets all ATX 3.1 requirements with traditional connectors.
Built on decades of engineering excellence, the CORE BC Series delivers the quiet efficiency and reliability that define every Seasonic power supply.
The 80 PLUS® Bronze certification indicates that a high percentage of the electricity is converted into useful power, therefore there is less heat lost and more money saved on the electricity bill.

Next-Gen and Legacy GPU Cable
Includes native 12V-2x6 and 2× 8-pin cables for maximum compatibility
Optimized for PCIe 5.1 GPUs
The CORE BC ATX 3.1 power supply features a native 12V-2x6 cable designed for the latest PCIe 5.1 graphics cards. With support for up to 600 W of power delivery (see below), this cable ensures safe and stable performance for NVIDIA RTX 40 and 50 Series and future high-end GPUs. Enjoy a clean, efficient setup that’s fully compliant with ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 standards.
Fully compliant with PCIe 5.1 and ATX 3.1 standards
12V-2x6 Cable: Up to 450 W power delivery for the 750 W.
12V-2x6 Cable: Up to 600 W power delivery for the 850 W.
The CORE BC-650 complies with ATX 3.1 specifications but is supplied with traditional PCIe connectors instead of a 12V-2x6 cable.
Full Support for Legacy GPUs
To ensure compatibility with older GPUs, the CORE BC ATX 3.1 includes a 2× 8-pin PCIe cable. It delivers reliable power up and works seamlessly with graphics cards from previous generations. This cable makes it easy to upgrade your PSU without changing your GPU—perfect for users who want next-gen power with legacy support.
Dual 8-pin PCIe connectors for broad compatibility
Ideal for graphics cards from previous generations
Easy to install for users upgrading from older systems
Reliable support for legacy GPU power requirements
S2FC - Intelligent Fan Control Technology
The Smart and Silent Fan Control (S2FC) system intelligently regulates the power supply’s fan speed to achieve the ideal balance between cooling efficiency and silent operation. By dynamically adjusting the fan curve according to temperature, it ensures that your system remains quiet during low-to-medium usage and effectively cooled when performance demands increase.

FAQ
What kind of system is CORE BC designed for?
CORE BC is the more straightforward entry point in the current CORE family. It combines ATX 3.1 support, fixed cabling and 650 W, 750 W or 850 W output options with an 80 PLUS Bronze efficiency rating. It is aimed at everyday gaming and general-purpose builds where the extra features of the higher series are not required.
What is the difference between 80 PLUS Bronze and Gold?
Both are efficiency certifications, but Gold requires higher conversion efficiency at the defined certification load points than Bronze. This mainly affects how much input power is lost as heat; it does not by itself describe every other aspect of PSU performance. For a closer look at the efficiency tiers, see our guide to 80 PLUS certification.
Do all CORE BC models include the same 12V-2×6 cable?
No. This is one of the important differences within the range. CORE BC-850 includes a 12V-2×6 connection rated for up to 600 W, while BC-750 provides up to 450 W through its 12V-2×6 cable. CORE BC-650 remains ATX 3.1 compliant but uses traditional PCIe 8-pin connectors instead.
Is the fixed-cable design a disadvantage?
Not necessarily. If the included cables match your system, fixed cabling keeps the PSU simple and avoids having to select modular cables. The trade-off is that unused cables cannot be removed. If full modularity is important for cable management, CORE GX is the better fit.
Which CORE BC wattage should I buy?
Start with the hardware rather than the PSU number. A 650 W system does not automatically need 750 W just because a larger model exists, while a more demanding GPU may require both additional wattage and a particular connector configuration. Check the complete build before choosing between 650 W, 750 W and 850 W. For more information on what PSU you should get, use our Wattage Calculator.

What kind of system is CORE BC designed for?
CORE BC is the more straightforward entry point in the current

. It combines ATX 3.1 support, fixed cabling and 650 W, 750 W or 850 W output options with an 80 PLUS Bronze efficiency rating. It is aimed at everyday gaming and general-purpose builds where the extra features of the higher series are not required.
What is the difference between 80 PLUS Bronze and Gold?

Both are efficiency certifications, but Gold requires higher conversion efficiency at the defined certification load points than Bronze.
